requirements.title: Full-database backup/restore incl. persisted ledgers (disaster recovery)
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: The provider-based backup (backup.ts) only exports tables that own a Repository, silently omitting the engine-written persisted ledgers (stock_ledger_entries/stock_balances, journal_entries/journal_lines, fiscal_events, efactura_submissions, productie_mobila) — a restore would lose the entire posted financial history (a DR hole). exportBazaSql snapshots the WHOLE database, discovering tables from sqlite_master so any future table is captured automatically (cannot be forgotten from a hand-written list); _migrations is excluded (schema is re-applied on the target before restore). importBazaSql restores atomically in one transaction with FK checks deferred to commit, so delete/insert order — including the documente→documente self-reference — is irrelevant, and any failure rolls back leaving the target untouched. Optional integrity gate (verificaIntegritateBackup) rejects a restore whose journal is unbalanced. Verified on real SQLite: +7 in @gr/data (ledger tables captured; byte-for-byte round-trip into a fresh migrated DB; self-ref restored under active FK; replace-mode wipes pre-existing rows; balanced-journal verification; unbalanced/corrupt backup rejected with rollback) and +1 end-to-end in @gr/application (post a REAL document → snapshot → restore into a new DB → documente/linii/stock/journal/fiscal row counts identical, stock balance 98, brut 24200, journal balanced). Suite 361->369 passed / 1 skipped.
risks: SQLite-focused: table discovery uses sqlite_master and restore uses PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys (the desktop/local + demo path). A PostgreSQL deployment should back up via pg_dump / PITR; a PG-native exporter is not yet implemented.

Snapshot is a full JSON dump held in memory — fine for SME-scale DBs; a streaming/chunked exporter would be needed for very large datasets. No encryption-at-rest or off-site rotation of the snapshot file yet (operational runbook concern, Phase 17).

requirements.title: Restore-verified backup CLI + CI DR drill + DR runbook
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Turns the P16 snapshot into an operational DR capability that proves itself. backupVerificat (in @gr/data, node-free via an injected scratch-executor factory so the web bundle is unaffected) exports then immediately restores into a fresh scratch DB and asserts per-table row-count fidelity + a balanced journal before returning the snapshot — a corrupt/incomplete backup throws (BackupCorruptError) instead of being trusted. The @gr/server backup-cli.ts exposes backup/restore/verify over SQLite files, each wrapped with a SHA-256 checksum; restore verifies the checksum and refuses an unbalanced journal, and is atomic (rolls back on failure). A CI dr-drill job runs the WHOLE procedure on every push (seed posted data -> backup -> restore into a NEW DB -> assert integrity), so a regression in the backup/restore path breaks the build — not just unit-mocked. A DR_RUNBOOK.md documents schedule, encryption/off-site/retention, tested restore, and the PostgreSQL pg_dump/PITR path. Verified on real SQLite (+2 @gr/data, +4 @gr/server; drill green locally, exit 0). Suite 369->375 passed / 1 skipped.
risks: SQLite-focused (desktop/local). A PostgreSQL-native exporter mirroring backupVerificat is not implemented; the server path relies on pg_dump/PITR (documented in the runbook).

Backup encryption at rest, off-site rotation and the backup SCHEDULE are operational policy, not yet automated in-product (the tooling only guarantees a proven-restorable file). Signed installer/updater for desktop remains open under Phase 17 ops scope.
requirements.externalValidation: CI DR drill runs on GitHub Actions (Linux); cannot be executed inside this sandbox but is exercised on push.

requirements.title: UI posts documents through authoritative commands (network mode)

Validating a document in the UI was a generic CRUD state flip (db.documente.update(id, {stare:'validat'})) that bypassed the engine. Now createCommandClient (@gr/data) posts to /commands/<name> with the live session token and surfaces server business errors (409/423/...) as their message; useComenzi (@gr/ui) returns it in network mode / null in local mode; DocumentEditor's validate action + save(validate) write the document as a CIORNA then call posteaza() when the command client exists (local demo keeps the direct flip, having no engine). Verified LIVE in the Browser preview: demo server on real in-memory SQLite (full engine) + UI in LAN mode (admin/admin123); creating+validating a plus/minus document produced exactly POST /numerotare/next -> POST /documente (201 ciorna) -> POST /documente_linii -> POST /commands/post-document (200), and the row shows 'validat'. 4 unit tests (mock fetch) + the memory-demo DocumentEditor test unchanged. Suite 375->379 passed / 1 skipped.

Reverse-document command client exists (storneaza) but no UI action yet.

Demo-seed defect surfaced during verification (pre-existing, not from this change): the numbering allocator (serii_documente) is not seeded to match pre-seeded documents, so the first create of an already-seeded document type collides on ux_documente_numar (500). Tracked separately.

(b) Accounting reports off the persisted ledger: journal-repo listeazaNoteContabilePersistate groups journal_entries+journal_lines into NotaContabila[]; @gr/data createReportsClient + @gr/ui useRapoarte fetch GET /reports/journal (firma-scoped, contabilitate.vizualizare); useContabilitate reads the persisted registru in network mode (recompute fallback local), so ALL accounting pages (registru-jurnal, cartea mare, balanta, fisa) reflect the ledger the engine wrote, not a client recompute. requirements.title: Stock reports read the persisted stock ledger (network mode)

requirements.title: Offline command queue wired into the client command transport
tests: live browser E2E (LAN mode): offline enqueue
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: Authoritative commands (post/reverse/approve/cancel) were fire-and-fail on a flaky connection; the tested @gr/sync offline-queue primitives were unwired. They now go through @gr/data createOfflineCommandClient which wraps the command client: when the server is unreachable the command is enqueued (persisted in localStorage via stocatorStorage) with a stable idempotency key and ComandaInCoadaError is raised; on reconnect (window 'online' + on mount) the queue is replayed via comenziDeReluat, and the server's Phase-4 idempotency means a double replay never double-posts. Business errors (4xx) still surface — only transport failures queue. useComenzi returns the offline client and auto-replays, toasting sent/rejected counts; DocumentEditor validate/storno/save catch ComandaInCoadaError -> info toast. +8 @gr/data tests. Suite 392->400 passed / 1 skipped. Verified LIVE (LAN mode): online post/storno unchanged; with api-server STOPPED a storno enqueued the exact reverse-document command in gr-coada-comenzi (idempotency key reverse-document:<docId>:-:2026-08-09:, payload, executate:[]).
risks: Only COMMANDS are queued; writing a NEW draft in network mode still needs the server (no local data persistence in network mode) — full offline data entry needs a browser SQLite engine (separate work). The win is post/storno of an ALREADY-persisted document surviving intermittent connectivity without double-posting.
Reconnect-replay is unit-tested, not live-verified: the in-memory demo server resets its DB + session secret on restart, so a live SUCCESSFUL replay isn't reproducible in this harness.
reconcileSigur (conflict-aware DATA reconciliation, RK-12) is NOT yet in the client sync loop — it needs a local dataset to reconcile against; applies once local persistence lands.
requirements.externalValidation: Offline replay/idempotency proven by @gr/data + @gr/sync unit tests; live browser E2E in-session only (enqueue path).

requirements.title: Browser SQLite executor (fromSqlJs) — engine runs on WASM (spike)
requirements.acceptanceEvidence: De-risks LOCAL (web) mode: running the SAME @gr/application engine + ledger reads offline with no server. fromSqlJs is a SqlExecutor over sql.js (SQLite in WebAssembly), contract-identical to fromBetterSqlite (execute/select/transaction with BEGIN + SAVEPOINT nesting, UNIQUE->ConstraintViolationError, TransactionUsageError after tx ends). Exposed via @gr/data/web-sqlite (NOT re-exported from the index, so WASM stays out of every bundle). Proven: 7 @gr/data contract tests (incl. the FULL real schema — all migrations — applying on WASM + generic-repo read-your-writes) and 1 @gr/application test where createDraftDocument+postDocument on fromSqlJs writes journal_lines+stock_ledger_entries+fiscal_events ATOMICALLY with the journal balanced (debit==credit) — same engine as the server, browser executor. Suite 403->411 passed / 1 skipped; typecheck 11/11; biome clean; build:web OK (sql.js absent from the web bundle).
risks: SPIKE only — NOT wired into the UI yet. Remaining integration: async provider init in data-context (LOCAL mode currently builds a synchronous in-memory provider), bundle the db/migrations SQL for the browser build, and persist the WASM DB to IndexedDB across reloads. Until then LOCAL mode still uses the memory provider (no engine).
sql.js is a synchronous single-writer WASM instance (like better-sqlite3) — fine for a single-user desktop/web client; not for multi-writer concurrency (that stays server/PostgreSQL).
WASM init is async and adds ~1-2 MB to the LOCAL-mode bundle when wired — acceptable for an offline-capable app, but a load path to design.
requirements.externalValidation: Contract parity + engine-on-WASM proven by @gr/data + @gr/application vitest suites (WASM runs in vitest). No browser E2E yet (integration pending).
